g.text: The pipeline begins with a sequence of video frames showing the robot workspace.
Subsequent frames capture the demonstration over time.
The top frame provides the reference image for tokenization and tracking.
The input video sequence is processed by a frozen off-the-shelf tracker.
The tracker extracts multi-point trajectories across consecutive visual frames.
These trajectory sequences are formatted into timelines containing masked points.
The first point timeline includes masked intermediate points across the time steps.
The second point track follows a similar masked sequence.
Likewise, the third track contains masked points across its timeline.
In parallel, image tokens are extracted directly from the initial frame.
A language instruction is also provided as input.
The instruction is mapped to a language token.
Each masked timeline is converted into an input track token.
This includes the token for the second point trajectory.
And the track token for the third trajectory.
The image tokens, language token, and track tokens are fed jointly into the Track Transformer.
The model outputs updated track tokens corresponding to the completed paths.
An updated track token is generated for the second path.
And for the third point track.
These tokens reconstruct the fully unmasked point trajectory from start to finish.
The second trajectory is fully reconstructed as well.
As is the complete third point trajectory.
At inference time, a language instruction is supplied.
The current visual observation frame is captured from the camera.
The instruction and observation are processed by the frozen Track Transformer.
This produces predicted point tracks overlaid across the scene.
Both the initial visual frame and predicted tracks enter the Track-guided Policy.
Finally, the policy outputs the predicted action for the robot.
